Stop using it now. If you can do it safely, switch it off at the socket or at the consumer unit (fuse box). A shock usually means an earth or insulation fault, so don't use it again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has found and fixed it. No, a tingle is not normal and indicates a potential earthing issue. This can happen if the socket isn't properly earthed or if there's stray voltage leaking from an internal component due to worn insulation. For your safety, please stop using the machine until we check this. The most common cause is simply that the wall socket doesn't have a good earth connection. No, that is not normal. A tingle means there is stray voltage on the casing, usually because the earthing isn't doing its job properly. Do not use the machine again until a qualified appliance engineer or electrician has checked the socket's earth connection and the machine's internal wiring. Using an extension lead for high-draw appliances like washing machines can also mask earthing issues, so once fixed, plug it directly into a wall socket.
